about.faq.title: Common questions
about.faq.subtitle: Quick answers to the things people ask most.
about.faq.free.a: Yes, Webtor.io is completely free for basic use. You can stream and download torrents without creating an account. Optional paid plans remove ads, increase bandwidth, and unlock Vault cloud storage.
about.faq.vpn.q: Do I need a VPN to use Webtor.io? Will my ISP see what I download?
about.faq.vpn.a: No VPN required. All traffic between you and Webtor.io travels over HTTPS. Your IP address is never exposed to the BitTorrent network because Webtor.io servers handle all peer communication. For your ISP, using Webtor.io looks no different from visiting any other website.
about.faq.mobile.q: Can I use Webtor.io on a phone or tablet?
about.faq.mobile.a: Yes. Webtor.io works in any modern mobile browser on iOS and Android. You can stream video, listen to audio, and download torrents without installing any additional apps.
about.faq.formats.q: What video and audio formats does Webtor.io support?
about.faq.formats.a: Webtor.io supports instant streaming for most popular formats. Video: AVI, MKV, MP4, WEBM, M4V, TS, VOB. Audio: MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, M4A. Files that require transcoding may take a moment longer to start playing.
about.faq.opensource.a: Yes, 100%. All components of Webtor.io are distributed under the MIT license. You can visit the GitHub repository to view the source code and contribute.
about.faq.smarttv.q: Can I watch my library on a smart TV?
about.faq.smarttv.a: Yes! With the Stremio integration you can stream your personal library on any smart TV or device running Stremio. Just install the addon using the link from your profile.
about.faq.indexers.q: Can I use my own Jackett or Prowlarr with Webtor?
about.faq.indexers.a: Yes. Add your indexer's Torznab feed URL in your profile and its results appear next to your Stremio addons — both on the Discover page and in the Webtor Stremio addon. Webtor doesn't search anything itself; it plays what your own indexer returns.
about.faq.releaseSubs.q: Can Webtor tell me when a new episode or release comes out?
about.faq.releaseSubs.a: Yes. Subscribe to an airing season or a movie — from the Discover page or a torrent page — and Webtor will poll your connected indexers and Stremio addons, then email you when a new release appears. It works like Sonarr or RSS automation, but with nothing to host.
about.faq.openTorrent.q: How do I open a .torrent file in my browser?
about.faq.openTorrent.a: Drag your .torrent file into the upload area at the top of this page, or paste a magnet link into the search field. Webtor opens it instantly — pick the video or audio file you want and stream it, or grab a direct download link. There's no torrent client to install and nothing to set up.
about.faq.magnetDownload.q: How do I download files from a magnet link without a torrent client?
about.faq.magnetDownload.a: Paste the magnet link into the search field at the top of this page. Webtor acts as an online magnet link downloader: it runs the magnet download in the cloud and gives you a direct HTTP download link for each file, plus a built-in player to stream video and audio. Your browser never connects to the BitTorrent network — Webtor servers handle that.
about.faq.magnetUse.q: How do I use a magnet link?
about.faq.magnetUse.a: Paste the magnet link into the search field at the top of this page — Webtor opens it in seconds, with no client to install. You can also drag and drop a .torrent file instead. Webtor fetches the data on its own servers, so your browser never joins the BitTorrent swarm; you simply stream or download the files.
about.faq.openTorrentApp.q: What can I use to open a torrent file?
about.faq.openTorrentApp.a: You don't need to install anything — Webtor opens torrent files right in your browser on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, and iOS. Upload the .torrent file or paste a magnet link, then stream the video or save the files over a regular HTTPS download. Desktop clients like qBittorrent or uTorrent also work, but they require installation and connect your device to the torrent swarm.
about.faq.unzipTorrent.q: How do I unzip a torrent file?
about.faq.unzipTorrent.a: A .torrent file is not an archive, so there is nothing to unzip — it's a small metadata file that only describes the real content. To get the actual files, open the .torrent with Webtor and download them one by one, or use the Torrent to ZIP tool to download everything as a single ZIP or TAR archive.
about.faq.downloadTorrented.q: How do I download torrented files without a torrent client?
about.faq.downloadTorrented.a: Paste a magnet link or upload a .torrent file at the top of this page. Webtor fetches the torrent on its servers and gives you a direct HTTPS download link for every file — nothing to install, and it works on any device. Your browser never joins the BitTorrent swarm, so no open ports or client setup are needed.
about.faq.aiDiscover.q: What is Discover and how do the AI recommendations work?
about.faq.aiDiscover.a: Discover is a recommendations page powered by AI. Open it from the main navigation, type what you want to watch (or tap one of the suggested chips), and Webtor returns a personalized list of films — each with a short reason explaining why it fits your taste and what you've watched before. Click any card to start streaming through your usual addons.
about.faq.aiQuota.q: Is AI Discover free? How many requests do I get?
about.faq.aiQuota.a: Yes — every account gets {{.FreeQuota}} free AI request(s) per day. Supporters of the project get {{.PaidQuota}} requests per day. Suggestion chips and the rest of the Discover catalog are unlimited; only the natural-language search counts against the daily quota.
about.faq.aiModel.q: What AI model powers the recommendations? Is my data safe?
about.faq.aiModel.a: Recommendations are generated by Anthropic's Claude — a fast model for the free tier and a more capable one for supporters. We send the model only your title/year/rating history. No email, IP address, or any other personal data is shared. The response is used purely to suggest films you can stream through your usual addons.
about.faq.expire.q: Do download links or streams expire?
about.faq.expire.a: Yes, for security reasons direct download links and streaming sessions are temporary and may expire after a short time. You can always refresh or regenerate them from your library interface.
about.faq.ads.q: How can I remove ads on Webtor.io?
about.faq.ads.a: Support the project and you'll get an ad-free experience, faster loading speeds, and a heart icon in the interface.
about.faq.zip.q: Why do some downloaded ZIP archives show a CRC error?
about.faq.zip.a: ZIP archives are generated on-the-fly and don't include full checksum data, so some extraction tools may show a CRC warning even when the file is intact. That's why directory downloads now default to TAR — the TAR format has no per-file checksums, so even an interrupted and resumed download unpacks cleanly. If you prefer ZIP, pick it from the arrow menu next to the download button and use 7-Zip for best compatibility.
about.faq.speed.q: Why is my download or streaming speed slow on Webtor.io?
about.faq.speed.a1: Speeds may vary due to the number of seeders, file format (some require real-time transcoding), your internet connection, current server load, and your account type. Premium users get higher bandwidth.
about.faq.streamVsDownload.q: Torrent streaming vs direct download — what's the difference?
about.faq.streamVsDownload.a: A direct download makes you wait for the whole file before you can watch it. Webtor streams the torrent instead: playback starts in seconds and nothing piles up on your device — and when you do want a local copy, you can still save the file as a regular download.
about.faq.streamVsDownload.link: Read the full comparison on our blog
about.faq.speed.a2: Note: bandwidth is measured in Mbps (megabits per second), while file sizes are shown in MB (megabytes). 1 MB = 8 Mb, so a 50 Mbps connection gives roughly 6.25 MB/s download speed. Supporting the project helps unlock better speed and reliability.

tool.torrentToMp4.about.explained.title: Why "torrent to MP4" has nothing to convert
tool.torrentToMp4.about.explained.p1: A .torrent file holds no video at all. It is a small index: the names and sizes of the files, their checksums, and where to find the peers that have them. Converting it to MP4 makes as much sense as converting a library catalogue into a book — the thing you want is not in there yet.
tool.torrentToMp4.about.explained.p2: The video arrives when the torrent is actually downloaded, and it arrives in whatever container the release used — usually MP4 or MKV, sometimes AVI. Webtor.io skips the middle step: it fetches the torrent in the cloud, shows you the files inside, and plays the video in the browser while it downloads. Nothing to install, nothing to convert.

tool.openTorrentFile.about.explained.p1: A .torrent file contains no content at all. It is an index: the names and sizes of the files, checksums to verify them by, and the trackers that know who currently has them. That is why double-clicking it does nothing useful until something can read it.
tool.openTorrentFile.about.explained.p2: The usual answer is to install a BitTorrent client. It works, but it means software on your machine, a download that must finish before you can watch anything, and your own connection sharing the data with strangers.
tool.openTorrentFile.about.explained.p3: Webtor.io reads the file on the server instead. You get the same contents listing in seconds, and playback starts before the download is anywhere near finished — because the video is streamed to you rather than assembled on your disk.

One file or the whole torrent, by ordinary download link — no client, no queue, no seeding afterwards.
Upload a .torrent file or paste a magnet link into Webtor.io.

Save it like any other file, or grab the whole torrent as a single archive.
tool.howToDownloadTorrentFiles.about.exp: Why a torrent normally makes this hard

A torrent is not a download link. It is a list of pieces spread across other people's computers, which is why a client has to collect them, verify them and reassemble the file before you have anything you can use.

That is fine when the swarm is healthy and you wanted everything. It is a poor deal when you needed one episode out of forty, or when the client will keep uploading from your connection long after you are done.

Webtor.io does the collecting on the server and hands you an ordinary HTTP link. Your browser downloads it the way it downloads anything else — resumable, one file at a time if you like, and finished when the file is on your disk.

tool.openTorrentsOnPc.about.explained.p2: On a work laptop, a school computer or a machine you do not administer, that is the end of the road: installers are blocked, and so, often, is the BitTorrent protocol itself.

tool.torrentToDdl.about.explained.title: What is torrent to DDL and how does it work?
tool.torrentToDdl.about.explained.p1: Torrent to DDL is a method of converting a torrent file into a direct download link (DDL) that works over standard HTTP or HTTPS. Instead of connecting to peers through a torrent client, the torrent is processed on a server and the files become available as regular downloadable links.
tool.torrentToDdl.about.explained.p2: This approach removes the need to install torrent software and makes downloading or streaming files easier on any device, including mobile phones and tablets.

tool.torrentToDdl.about.compare.subtitle: Torrents and direct download links both deliver files, but they use very different technologies.
tool.torrentToDdl.about.compare.footer: Torrent to DDL is often preferred when you want simplicity, stability, and quick access to files without dealing with torrent clients.
tool.torrentToDdl.about.safety.title: Is torrent to DDL safe? Do I need a VPN?
tool.torrentToDdl.about.safety.text: Torrent to DDL is generally safer than using a traditional torrent client because you do not connect directly to the torrent swarm. Your IP address is not exposed to other peers in the same way. All traffic between you and Webtor.io travels over HTTPS, so no VPN is required.
tool.torrentToDdl.about.video.title: Why torrent to DDL is better for video files
tool.torrentToDdl.about.video.subtitle: Video torrents are often inconvenient with classic torrent clients: you may need to wait for enough pieces to download before playback works smoothly. With torrent to DDL, video files can be streamed over HTTP, so you can start watching instantly without downloading the entire file first.
tool.torrentToDdl.about.video.footer: If your torrent contains video content, streaming is usually faster and more convenient than downloading everything upfront.
tool.torrentToDdl.about.faq.q1.question: How do I convert a torrent to a direct download link?
tool.torrentToDdl.about.faq.q1.answer: Upload your torrent file or paste a magnet link into Webtor.io. The torrent is processed on our servers and each file becomes available as a regular HTTPS link you can download or stream — no installation, no extra steps.

tool.stremioAddonsOnline.about.explained: What are Stremio addons and how do they work online?

Stremio addons are small web services that provide catalogs, metadata and stream sources — including torrent streams — for the Stremio media center. Normally they require the Stremio app installed on your device.

Webtor.io speaks the same addon protocol, so the addons you already use in Stremio work online too: Webtor queries them for torrent sources and plays the result in its cloud player with real-time HLS transcoding — any format, any browser.
Why use Stremio addons in the browser?
The Stremio app has to be installed, and on many devices its torrent streaming is limited or unavailable. Webtor turns any browser into a Stremio-compatible player.
No Stremio installation — everything works online
All your addon catalogs and torrent sources in one place
Torrents play in the cloud — your device never joins the swarm
Works even where the Stremio app can’t stream torrents, like iPhone and iPad
tool.stremioAddonsOnline.about.safety.ti: Is it safe to use Stremio addons online?
tool.stremioAddonsOnline.about.safety.te: Yes. You choose which addons to connect, and Webtor.io talks to them server-side. Torrent data is fetched by Webtor’s cloud and delivered to your browser over encrypted HTTPS — no VPN needed, no ports to open, and no peer-to-peer traffic touches your network.
tool.stremioAddonsOnline.about.devices.s: Anything with a modern browser becomes a Stremio-compatible streaming player — and with the personal Webtor addon the integration also works the other way around, inside Stremio itself.
tool.stremioAddonsOnline.about.devices.i: iPhones and iPads via Safari or Chrome — where the Stremio app can’t play torrents
Smart TVs — add the personal Webtor addon to Stremio and stream your library there

instructions.stremio.title: Stremio Integration
instructions.stremio.heading: How to connect Webtor to Stremio
instructions.stremio.intro: You can stream your personal torrent library from Webtor directly in Stremio. Here's how to do it:
instructions.stremio.quick: Fastest way: press Install in Stremio in your Webtor profile — the Stremio app opens and adds the addon by itself. If that did not work (no app installed, Stremio Web, another device), the manual way:
instructions.stremio.step1: Copy your personal addon link from your Webtor profile.
instructions.stremio.step2: Open Stremio and go to the Add-ons section.
instructions.stremio.step3: Click the Add Addon button in the top-right corner.
instructions.stremio.step4: Paste the addon link and press Enter. Done!
instructions.stremio.result: Once installed, your library will appear in Stremio under the Webtor.io addon – ready to stream.
instructions.stremio.noteWarmup: Streaming via Webtor may differ from regular Stremio addons. It can take some time to warm up the torrent before playback starts.
instructions.stremioAddon.title: How to connect Stremio Addon
instructions.stremioAddon.heading: How to connect Stremio Addon
instructions.stremioAddon.intro: Want to add more content to your Stremio experience? Follow these simple steps to connect external Stremio addons to expand your streaming library:
instructions.stremioAddon.step1: Go to stremio-addons.com
instructions.stremioAddon.step2: Browse and select the addon you want to install
instructions.stremioAddon.step3: Copy the addon's manifest URL with the "Copy link" button
instructions.stremioAddon.step4: Paste the URL in the "Stremio Addons" section at your profile page and click "Add Addon"
instructions.stremioAddon.result: Once added, the addon content will be available through your Stremio integration, expanding your streaming options with additional sources and catalogs.
instructions.stremioAddon.noteGathering: Gathering streaming URLs can take some time (up to 10 seconds). Be patient.
instructions.torznab.title: How to connect a torrent indexer
instructions.torznab.heading: How to connect a torrent indexer
instructions.torznab.intro: A Torznab indexer is a search endpoint for torrent trackers — Jackett, Prowlarr and NZBHydra2 all expose one, and some trackers speak Torznab directly. Connect yours to Webtor and its results appear next to your Stremio addon results, so your own trackers become just another source of streams.
instructions.torznab.step1: Set up the tracker you want in Jackett or Prowlarr, and make sure its search works there.
instructions.torznab.step2: Copy the Torznab feed URL. In Jackett press Copy Torznab Feed next to a configured indexer, or take the link of the all aggregate indexer to search every tracker at once. In Prowlarr open the indexer settings and copy its Torznab URL.
instructions.torznab.step3: Paste the URL into the "Torrent indexers" section on your profile page and click "Add".
instructions.torznab.step4: Leave the API key field empty if the copied URL already contains apikey= — that is the usual case. Fill it in only for feeds that do not embed the key.
instructions.torznab.result: From then on, results from your indexer show up in the stream list on Discover and in the Webtor Stremio addon, side by side with your Stremio addon results. Reordering, switching an indexer off and deleting it are all done on the profile page.
instructions.torznab.noteReachable: Webtor queries the indexer from its own servers, so its address must be reachable from the public internet. A local address like http://192.168.1.5:9117 will not work — publish the indexer on a domain or through a tunnel first. Local addresses only work on a self-hosted Webtor.
instructions.torznab.noteHttps: Prefer an HTTPS address: the API key travels inside the feed URL, so a plain HTTP endpoint exposes it on the way to your indexer.

instructions.webdav.step2: Install a WebDAV client on your device (see recommendations below).

instructions.s3.title: S3 Integration
instructions.s3.heading: How to connect Webtor via S3
instructions.s3.intro: Your library also speaks the S3 protocol, so any S3 client can browse and stream it. The folders are the same ones you get over WebDAV, exposed as buckets.
instructions.s3.step1: Copy the endpoint, access key and secret key from your Webtor profile.
instructions.s3.step2: Set up any S3 client with those credentials and path-style addressing.
instructions.s3.step3: Browse the buckets and stream your files.
instructions.s3.rcloneUsage: Then rclone lsd webtor: lists your buckets and rclone mount webtor:all /mnt/webtor mounts the library.

instructions.vault.title: Vault
instructions.vault.vpSource: Points are provided as part of your subscription or other activities (the amount depends on your subscription tier)
instructions.vault.howStep1: Click the "Keep This Torrent Available" button next to the torrent you want to save.
instructions.vault.howStep2: Confirm the number of points required (for example, if the torrent is 10 GB, you need to deposit 10 VP).
instructions.vault.howStep3: The funded points are frozen for {{.FreezePeriod}} after the pledge is created.
instructions.vault.howStep4: Webtor transfers the torrent to the Vault (if the transfer fails within {{.TransferTimeout}}, VP is returned).
instructions.vault.claimItem1: Points can be claimed back if they are not frozen.
instructions.vault.claimItem2: If after claiming points back the amount is less than required to keep the torrent, it will be marked as expired and deleted after {{.ExpirePeriod}}.
instructions.vault.claimItem3: When a torrent is deleted, all pledges associated with it are also deleted.
instructions.vault.expireItem1: Points that were invested in torrents lose their power and the torrent is marked as expired and deleted after {{.ExpirePeriod}}.
instructions.vault.expireItem2: If the subscription is renewed, the points become active again and the torrents funded by them are no longer expired.
instructions.vault.disclaimer: If a torrent is blocked by copyright holders or removed from public sources, it may disappear – Vault does not guarantee preservation in such cases.
aboutPage.title: About — Mission & Open Source
aboutPage.description: Webtor is an open-source, browser-based torrent platform. Learn about our mission to make torrents accessible, private, and easy to use — no installs required.
aboutPage.heading: About Webtor
aboutPage.intro: Webtor is a free, open-source platform that lets you stream and download torrents directly in the browser — no software to install, no configuration needed.
aboutPage.missionP1: Torrents are a powerful, decentralized way to share files — but using them has always required dedicated software, technical knowledge, and patience. We built Webtor to change that.
aboutPage.missionP2: Our goal is to make torrents accessible to everyone. Whether you want to stream a video, preview files before downloading, or just grab a single file from a torrent — you can do it all in your browser, on any device.
aboutPage.missionP3: Webtor processes everything in the cloud, so your device stays light and your IP stays private. No sign-up required — just paste a magnet link or upload a .torrent file and go.
aboutPage.osP1: Webtor is fully open-source under the MIT License. Every component — from the backend services to this web interface — is publicly available on GitHub.
aboutPage.osP2: We believe that transparency builds trust. You can inspect the code, report issues, suggest features, or contribute directly.

tool.cloudTorrentClient.title: Cloud Torrent Client
tool.cloudTorrentClient.benefit: Download & Stream Torrents in the Cloud
tool.cloudTorrentClient.description: A cloud torrent client that downloads torrents on Webtor's servers: paste a magnet link, stream while it downloads or save files over HTTPS. Your device never joins the swarm.
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.steps.titl: How the cloud torrent client works
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.steps.subt: Three steps, nothing to install — the heavy lifting happens on Webtor's servers, not on your device.
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.steps.step: Drop the file or link on the home page. The cloud client picks it up and connects to the BitTorrent swarm within seconds.
Peers, trackers and uploads stay on our side. No client to configure, no port forwarding, and nothing torrent-related runs on your device.
Play video right in the browser while the torrent downloads, or save any file through a plain HTTPS link — like downloading from an ordinary website.
What is a cloud torrent client?

A cloud torrent client is a torrent program that runs on remote servers instead of your computer. You hand it a magnet link or .torrent file, it joins the swarm and downloads the content, then serves the files back to you over HTTP — so to your device and your network, torrenting looks like ordinary web traffic.

Webtor is a cloud torrent client wrapped in a player: it downloads in the cloud and streams video on the fly, converts audio, loads subtitles and hands out direct download links. Torrents you add are saved to a personal library, and paid plans add long-term Vault storage, S3 and WebDAV access to mount the library as a drive, and a REST API to script all of it.
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.benefits.s: Everything a desktop client does, minus the parts that make torrenting painful.
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.benefits.i: Your device never joins the swarm, and other peers never see your IP address
No software and no configuration — works in any browser on any OS
Downloads run on data-center bandwidth; you only fetch what you actually watch or save
Streaming starts in seconds, with subtitles and audio-track selection built in
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.devices.su: Whatever the cloud client downloads lands in your library — and the library follows you around.
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.devices.it: Watch in the browser on desktop, phone or tablet, or on a TV through the Stremio addon
Mount the library as a network drive over WebDAV or S3 and browse it like local folders
Automate it with the REST API: add torrents, list files and get stream links from your own code
Pledge favourites to the Vault to keep them available long-term
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.safety.tit: Is a cloud torrent client safe?
tool.cloudTorrentClient.about.safety.tex: Safer than torrenting locally: nothing gets installed, other peers see Webtor's servers instead of your IP address, and everything reaches you over HTTPS. Webtor only processes torrents you add yourself — it is a player and downloader for your own content, not a content catalog.
